correctness.rationale: The facet area times the absolute normal component gives sqrt(m)/(m-2)! times |u_i|, before the factor 1/2 in Cauchy's formula. At a minimum, positive and negative coordinates each have total magnitude 1/sqrt(2), with exactly one coordinate of each sign. In the k=m-2 free tangent coordinates y, the Gram determinant is 1+k/2=m/2 and Z-sqrt(2)=||y||_1+O(||y||_1^2). The area of each near-minimum component is therefore sqrt(m/2) times the volume of a k-dimensional cross-polytope of radius t, with O(t^(k+1)) error. There are m(m-1) components. Within a sign chamber with r positive coordinates, the projected sign vector has norm 2 sqrt(r(m-r)/m); the largest norm is L_m and only the stated N_m chambers attain it. On any coordinate wall the value is at most D_m, and unbalanced chambers are bounded by E_m. Both bounds are strictly less than L_m for m>=3. A cap above these two bounds cannot leave its chamber: at a first wall crossing along a shortest geodesic the chamber's linear functional still agrees with Z. Area integration gives (3), and sigma_(k-1)/k=kappa_k gives the leading coefficient of (2). At m=3 the six caps meet only on boundaries at the minimum and the derivative of the exact circle law there agrees with (1). The analytical reconstruction does not rely on the inspected seeded simulation. The supplied replay path is check_brightness.py; it was not executed.
